summary: Initial discovery for Infradata's retrieval+rerank architecture. Customer wants to understand tradeoffs between embedding dimensionality, host options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and how Redwood integrates with their vector DB. Main concerns: throughput (1k QPS target), tail latency for rerank, security/VPC and cost. Agreed next steps: SE benchmark on dedicated-8, share security docs, pilot kickoff scheduling.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment implications
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03 16:00 PST
Length: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Infradata Head of Search), Tom Walters (Infra Lead), Jenna Lee (Data Eng)

Auto-summary (may be rough): Priya describes current retrieval stack: hybrid search that first fanouts to a vector DB then reranks top-k with a small encoder. They want to test Redwood in two modes: (1) Hosted API for quick proof-of-value and (2) Dedicated for production capacity guarantees; Private VPC considered for compliance. Key metrics: 1k QPS embedding generation + rerank with sub-200ms p95 across pipeline, cost per query, and storage size for 512-d embeddings.

[00:00] Alyssa Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll keep this 45 to 60, um, just to understand your workload and constraints. quick intros?
[00:10] Priya Nair: hi i'm priya, head of search at infradata. we ingest logs and docs, run embedding-based similarity first and then a rerank. our main pain is cost at scale and spikes in tail latency when reranking topk.
[00:22] Tom Walters: tom here, infra lead. we're mostly on k8s in a multi-AZ cloud account, need VPC peering and tight egress controls.
[00:30] Jenna Lee: jenna, data eng, i run the embedding pipeline, currently using a 384-d model we trained in-house, but open to switching to 256/512 depending on perf tradeoffs.
[00:40] Mateo Ruiz: great, i'm mateo from redwood se—i'll dive into throughput numbers and connector options. quick question: what's your typical query fanout and rerank top-k today?
[00:52] Priya Nair: average fanout 250 doc vectors, we then rerank top 12 results in the model. peak qps around 700 during business hours, want to plan for 1k plus burst. tail latency p95 from the reranker is like 450ms sometimes—too high.
[01:15] Alyssa Chen: thanks. sounds like two levers: reduce fanout via better recall/hybrid, or make rerank faster via quantized models or dedicated capacity. which of those are you open to experimenting with?
[01:30] Priya Nair: both. we tried shrinking embeddings to 128 but saw relevance drop; we want to find a sweet spot. also, curious how Redwood's caching and batching could help—especially kv cache for chat-like flows.
[01:45] Mateo Ruiz: quick note: our runtime supports continuous batching and prefix / KV caching, but for rerank use-cases it's usually about throughput of small-context generator models and latency of the reranker. for your 1k qps target: dedicated pools with optimized kernels and 8-bit quantization often hit that while keeping p95 under target, depending on sequence lengths.
[02:10] Tom Walters: when you say dedicated pools, is that Redwood Dedicated that we reserve? how isolated is it—like network access to our VPC?
[02:18] Alyssa Chen: yes, Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity. we offer private control plane for Private deployments with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, but Dedicated also has tenant isolation and options for private network links depending on contract. i'll send the exact network topologies in the security packet.
[02:36] Jenna Lee: can we bring our vector DB? we run Milvus clusters today; do you integrate or do we need to migrate to pinecone or your managed index?
[02:46] Mateo Ruiz: you can bring-your-own-DB. we have connectors and a lightweight SDK that can call your Milvus or Faiss endpoints. typical pattern: Redwood handles embedding generation and rerank, but vector DB remains your chosen store. for rerank-heavy flows we sometimes recommend moving top-k into a Redis or local cache to reduce fanout.
[03:10] Priya Nair: curious about dimensionality. if we move to 512-d versus our current 384-d, what's the storage and cost impact roughly?
[03:20] Mateo Ruiz: rough back-of-envelope: storage scales linearly with dim. 512 vs 384 is ~33% more storage. compute for similarity search may increase slightly, but reranker cost is independent. embeddings generation cost scales by sequence length and model; per-embedding cost is higher for larger models. but with quantization (8-bit or 4-bit) you can offset GPU memory so you can pack more models or batches.
[03:45] Tom Walters: what about hybrid search — we do lexical+vector. does Redwood help with reranker-aware recall to reduce fanout?
[03:52] Mate o Ruiz: (slight cough/mumble) sure, Redwood Optimize can suggest a hybrid config: use BM25 boosts + PNN-based re-ranking thresholds to lower average fanout. also we can run evals on your seed prompts to show recall vs fanout tradeoffs.
[04:15] Priya Nair: can you run a quick demo of a rerank pipeline? maybe a micro test that shows topk 12 rerank latency on dedicated vs hosted?
[04:23] Alyssa Chen: absolutely, that's part of the next steps. for hosted it's easiest but cost can be higher at scale; dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-query cost once committed. private gives full network control for compliance.
[04:40] Jenna Lee: any gotchas around KV cache or prefix caching when using our auth flows? we have short-lived tokens.
[04:48] Mateo Ruiz: cache keys respect request auth boundaries; for short-lived tokens we usually build a proxy to normalize identity and still allow safe prefix caching. we'll include recommended patterns.
[05:00] (background: muted chatter)
[05:20] Priya Nair: ok let's talk numbers: we need p95 end-to-end rerank under 200ms for interactive use cases, but batched analytics can be fine at 500ms. is that feasible?
[05:32] Mateo Ruiz: feasible on dedicated with optimized kernels and batching, assuming reranker sequence lengths are short (<=128 tokens) and you keep topk small. important to measure tail with realistic traffic bursts; we'll run smoke tests to show p50/p95/p99.
[06:00] Tom Walters: about security: do you support customer-managed KMS for Private? we need HSM-level key wrapping for certain datasets.
[06:08] Alyssa Chen: yes Private supports KMS integrations and HSM options via partner KMS. we'll include the SOC2 reports and KMS docs in the packet.
[06:18] Priya Nair: what about fallback if a dedicated node is overloaded? we want graceful degradation — how do you route to hosted variants?
[06:26] Mateo Ruiz: we have smart routing policies: route by latency/cost/region and fall back to compatible model variants in hosted fleet if Dedicated is saturated. you can set thresholds for automatic fallback.
[06:40] Jenna Lee: for the pilot, what data do you need from us? sample queries? full dataset?
[06:45] Alyssa Chen: sample queries, current index stats (cardinality, average docs per query), and a small production traffic replay if possible. Jenna, you mentioned sharing pipeline details — that will help us size the test.
[07:00] Priya Nair: we can provide a 10k query replay and a 1M vector index snapshot (sanitized).
[07:08] Mateo Ruiz: perfect. for benchmarks i'll run two scenarios: hosted inference with 256-d and 512-d embeddings and dedicated-8 pool with quantized reranker. we'll report costs, p50/p95/p99 and resource utilization.
[07:25] (short pause)
[07:40] Priya Nair: any limitations on model choices? our reranker is a distilled encoder (300M params) and we might want to run a 6B reranker for higher fidelity later.
[07:50] Mateo Ruiz: runtime supports a wide range; for 6B we recommend Dedicated or Private with proper GPU class. model quantization and kernel selection will be important; we'll advise on best perf profile.
[08:10] Tom Walters: how does billing look for embeddings-heavy workloads? per-embedding vs per-token?
[08:18] Alyssa Chen: hosted is usage-based: per-embedding generation cost (per vector) and per-token for generation models; Dedicated is commit-based with an effective lower unit cost and optional overage pricing. we'll put sample pricing in the follow-up.
[08:35] Jenna Lee: are there pre-built connectors to Milvus or do we run a shim?
[08:40] Mateo Ruiz: we have a connector for Milvus and a Faiss + file-based sink. typical approach: Redwood produces embeddings via API and a small sidecar writes vectors into your Milvus cluster. we can demo that.
[08:55] Priya Nair: ok let's recap next steps.
[09:00] Alyssa Chen: recap: (1) Mateo runs benchmarks (hosted 256/512, dedicated-8 quantized rerank) target 1k QPS burst and p95 measurements; (2) Alyssa sends security / VPC / KMS docs and pricing; (3) Jenna shares pipeline and sample data; (4) schedule pilot kickoff.
[09:20] Tom Walters: i'll coordinate internal calendar and we aim for week of 8/17.
[09:28] Priya Nair: and if benchmarks look good we'll scope a 6-8 week pilot with Dedicated and a Milvus connector.
[09:35] Alyssa Chen: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a calendar invite and deliverables.

(Transcript contains intermittent mis-transcriptions, e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache; speaker labels may flip in a few places.)

End of call.
